scope: Standing former Circuit House in Chittagong, now the Zia Memorial Museum.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Bangladesh National Museum confirms the former residence was built in 1913 by the British government, then converted into the memorial museum.
The 2016 physical survey in Table 2 identifies two storeys and brick masonry at S.S. Khaled Road.
The Bangladesh National Museum annual report describes the white exterior and its 3.17-acre hillside site.
The 2014 planning survey records occupation of the old Circuit House and distinguishes its location on a Chittagong hill.
The Ministry of Cultural Affairs identifies the Old Circuit House as the current museum building on the hill, built in 1913.
The 31 May 2025 first-hand site visit describes red roof tiles and tall windows.
The eyewitness material describes meetings on the Circuit House first-floor verandah in May 1981.

imageryScreen.localFinding: The CC0 photograph shows Ziaur Rahman at Schiphol. The local museum photographs are CC BY-SA and outside the imagery policy.
imageryScreen.supplementalFinding: The government press photograph of the October 2026 visit shows a museum room. It contains no exterior architecture to model.
